stories.headline: Donald Trump to raise nuclear-arms cuts with Putin, Xi on November 19, White House says
stories.deck: Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen
stories.bodyText:
U.S. President Donald Trump will raise nuclear-arms reduction at a meeting in China next week with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House said on Friday (November 13, 2026).
“He will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said on a call with reporters. She added that the meeting would take place on Thursday (November 19) in China.
Mr. Trump’s repeated insistence that the first-of-its-kind meeting of the three leaders focus on nuclear arms reductions has riled China, which is hosting a summit focused on trade and commerce. China has rebuffed attempts to talk about nuclear arms with Russia and the United States, which have the largest stockpiles of such weapons.
Mr. Putin, Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump are expected to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen. Mr. Trump is leaving on Monday (November 16) for a four-day trip to Asia that also includes a stop in the Philippines.
“We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement,” a senior Trump administration official said regarding the nuclear issue. “This is a difficult topic for China to address, but we do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things.”
The official added: “This is the beginning of hopefully a conversation that can be productive going forward.”
Beijing has for years resisted direct engagement with Washington about its nuclear program, saying it is more appropriate for Russia and the U.S. to speak directly because of their large arsenals.
Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired this year.
It was not clear whether Russia or China intended to engage in a conversation about arms reductions with Mr. Trump.
The Chinese and Russian embassies in Washington did not immediately respond to emailed requests for comment.
Trump will also raise the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran in the meeting but is not expected to raise Russia’s war in Ukraine, the official said.
The Republican president is not expected to have a one-on-one meeting with Mr. Putin or discuss Ukraine’s access to satellite communications service provided by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. Mr. Musk is joining Mr. Trump on the trip to China but will not attend his meeting with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin, according to the official.
“We’ve had many meetings recently with the Russians, but China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the person said.
Mr. Trump is also not expected to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his trip to Asia, according to the official.

stories.headline: Inside Amaravati’s pioneering leap to quantum frontier
stories.deck: The first major test vision of building an indigenous premier deep tech hub arrives soon as an IBM Quantum System, already en route from the U.S., will be installed on February 3, 2027, at Amaravati Quantum Valley; homegrown breakthroughs are already emerging from Amaravati 1Q and Amaravati 1S labs, led by Q SHIVA and NAADA
stories.bodyText:
For decades, advanced quantum hardware belonged exclusively to a handful of elite Western and East Asian laboratories. In this expensive, closed-off club, developing nations remained spectators or mere end users. In Amaravati, engineers and policymakers are working to upend that hierarchy. Starting from scratch, the Amaravati Quantum Valley (AQV) is turning a greenfield blueprint into South Asia’s premier deep tech hub, betting that India shouldn’t just use quantum computers; it should build them.
That ambition traces back to Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, whose push for frontier technology in Amaravati looked well beyond buying a foreign supercomputer. When shaping the project, an initiative backed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Naidu insisted that simply importing a machine would fall short; Andhra Pradesh needed a self-sustaining hardware ecosystem built from the ground up.

stories.headline: 'CA didn't interview Hazlewood, Starc': Warner’s explosive claim in sandpaper twist
stories.deck: In another development in the controversy that rocked Australian cricket, Warner claimed that CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon during its investigation in the days after the Cape Town Test in 2018.
stories.bodyText:
Former Australia opener 
David Warner
 has accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning the governing body's investigation into the incident.
In another development in the controversy that rocked Australian cricket, Warner claimed that CA did not interview 
Josh Hazlewood
, 
Mitchell Starc
 or Nathan Lyon during its investigation in the days after the Cape Town Test in 2018.
Warner made the allegation in an Instagram post on Saturday, a day after accusing Test captain Pat Cummins of throwing Usman Khawaja under the bus following the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr.
His latest comments came a day after Cummins addressed the allegations made in Khawaja's book during a lengthy press conference. The Australia captain dismissed the claims as “complete and utter nonsense”.
“As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation,” Warner posted to Instagram.
“If that’s correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?
“It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea. 
That stinks of a cover up.”
The ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight after Khawaja made several claims while promoting his book, alleging that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the Cape Town Test.
Cummins rejected those claims on Friday, while CA has previously said it has no intention of reopening the investigation into the incident.
Warner had also responded to Cummins' comments on Friday afternoon, ahead of Australia's opening ODI of the summer against England. He said he felt "the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus".
The former Australia opener followed that up with another Instagram post on Saturday, questioning the way CA handled the investigation.
Warner and then captain Steve Smith were handed one-year bans by CA following the incident, while Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.

stories.headline: Why it's time to travel with your girl gang
stories.bodyText: Every year, Belagavi-based Jyotika Bhore, 51, and four other fellow teachers from her school plan and embark on a trip during school vacations. No family, no kids, just the five women and some bookings. Jyotika says, “There is something magical about travelling with your gang of girls. We rarely make elaborate plans. No responsibilities to juggle, no need to be anyone’s perfect version of ourselves. We just travel for spontaneous adventures and a lifetime of memories.” A girls’ getaway is much more than a holiday. It is a much-needed pause from the everyday roles of being a professional, partner, mother, daughter, or caregiver. For a few days, you get to simply be you. And sometimes, that is exactly what refreshes you to the core. Break from the everyday routine Between work pressures, caregiving, household responsibilities, and social obligations, women rarely get to decide how they spend their vacations. A holiday with friends offers a refreshing change. No fixed routines, no meal planning, no worrying about who’s doing what. You can wake up late and still enjoy a leisurely breakfast, spend hours by the pool or simply do nothing at all. The freedom to be gloriously unproductive is itself a luxury. These vacations can be with office colleagues, school or college friends, cousins or just women you are comfortable travelling with. Laughter: the best therapy Remember those college stories or office gossip? The embarrassing moments and inside jokes that never get old? A girls’ holiday brings them all back. From laughing uncontrollably over the silliest things to discussing life, relationships, careers and dreams, these conversations are wonderfully therapeutic. There is something comforting about being around people who understand your quirks and love you anyway, without being judgemental. That is what makes a huge difference. No filters, no explanations With your girl gang, you don’t have to put on a show. You can turn up without makeup, wear your oldest comfortable T-shirt and baggy pants, talk about your insecurities or celebrate your little victories. Your deepest thoughts find an outlet in late-night chats. There is no pressure to perform or impress. Your friends accept you just as you are. That’s one of the most underrated joys of female friendships. Rediscover yourself Travel has a way of bringing out different sides of our personalities. It’s life in a nutshell. Perhaps you discover that you love adventure sports. You may enjoy exploring unfamiliar streets or find that you are surprisingly good at navigating a new city. Away from familiar surroundings and everyday expectations, you get to reconnect with a core part of yourself that may have taken a backseat. Your friends, too, could be surprised to see this unfiltered side of you. Little adventure, loads of confidence Whether trekking up a hill, exploring a museum, dancing at a beach shack or navigating an unfamiliar town, shared adventures create a wonderful sense of accomplishment. You discover that growing older certainly doesn’t mean growing less adventurous! Make that trip happen You don’t need an exotic international destination, a five-star resort, or a perfectly coordinated itinerary. A weekend getaway, a road trip with you at the wheel, a beach holiday, or a cosy staycation can be equally rejuvenating. The secret is to travel with people whose company leaves you feeling refreshed and rejuvenated.

stories.headline: A taste of winter: Gajjak, Sandesh, Malaiyo & more
stories.bodyText: Here comes winter, long-awaited and much cherished. The season has its own culinary traditions and flavours. With the slightest dip in temperatures, Indian kitchens come alive with the aroma of nuts, jaggery and ghee. These recipes are rooted in the traditional practice of eating nutrient-rich ingredients that provide warmth and nourishment during the colder months. Here are six winter favourites you can recreate at home. Gajjak A winter staple in North India, particularly Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, Gajjak is rich in flavour and wonderfully crisp. And yes, it is easy to make too! . Ingredients (Serves 4) *1 cup white sesame seeds *¾ cup grated jaggery *1 tsp ghee *¼ tsp cardamom powder Method *Dry-roast the sesame seeds over low heat until fragrant and they begin to pop. Keep aside. *Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add jaggery and 1 tbsp water, and melt over low heat. *Cook until the syrup reaches the hard-crack stage. To test, drop a little syrup into cold water; it should turn brittle. *Add the sesame seeds and cardamom powder. Mix quickly. *Spread the mixture onto a greased plate or parchment paper and roll it out thinly while still warm. *Cut into squares before it hardens completely. Malaiyo Long before molecular gastronomy took over the world, India had its own cloud on a plate. Malaiyo is a seasonal speciality of Varanasi. Made from milk froth collected after leaving milk outdoors overnight in the winter chill, it has an extraordinarily light and airy texture. . Ingredients (Serves 4) *1 litre full-fat milk *½ cup fresh cream *½ cup powdered sugar (adjust to taste) *¼ tsp cardamom powder *A few strands of saffron *2 tbsp chopped pistachios and almonds Method *Boil the milk, simmer for 10 minutes and allow it to cool completely. *Mix in the cream and transfer to a wide, shallow vessel. *Traditionally, the milk is left overnight in the cool winter air, allowing a thick layer of cream and froth to form. For a home-friendly alternative, chill it thoroughly and use an electric whisk to whip the mixture until light and frothy. *Add powdered sugar, cardamom powder and saffron. Spoon the airy mixture into small bowls and garnish with chopped nuts. Serve immediately while chilled. Patisapta A much-loved delicacy during the Bengali harvest festival of Poush Parbon, Patisapta is a delicate, thin crepe filled with a sweet mixture of coconut, khoya and jaggery. Soft, mildly sweet and fragrant, it is a filling winter treat that brings families together. . Ingredients (Serves 4 – 8 crepes) For the crepes: *½ cup rice flour *¼ cup all-purpose flour *2 tbsp semolina *1½ cups milk *1 tbsp sugar For the filling: *1 cup grated coconut *½ cup khoya *½ cup grated jaggery *¼ tsp cardamom powder Method *Mix rice flour, all-purpose flour, semolina, milk and sugar to make a smooth, thin batter. Allow it to rest for 20 minutes. Add a pinch of salt, if desired. *In a pan, heat the grated coconut with jaggery and cook until the jaggery melts. *Add khoya and cardamom powder. Stir until the mixture thickens. *Heat a lightly greased non-stick pan. Pour in a ladleful of batter and spread it into a thin crepe. *Cook until set. Place a spoonful of filling along one edge and roll gently. *Cook for another minute and serve warm. Nolen Gur Sandesh Bengal's fragrant date palm jaggery, harvested during the colder months, comes alive when combined with fresh chenna (Indian cottage cheese). It transforms into Sandesh, a delicately sweet, melt-in-the-mouth dessert. Its distinctive caramel-like aroma and earthy sweetness make it one of Bengal's most treasured seasonal delicacies. . Ingredients (Serves 4 – 8 small pieces) *2 cups fresh chenna (made by curdling approximately 1 litre of milk) *½ cup grated Nolen Gur *¼ tsp cardamom powder *1 tsp ghee *Chopped pistachios for garnish Method *Knead the fresh chenna gently until smooth and free of lumps. *Heat a non-stick pan and add the chenna and grated Nolen Gur. *Cook over low heat, stirring continuously, until the mixture thickens and comes together. Do not overcook, as it will turn rubbery. *Add cardamom powder and allow the mixture to cool slightly. *Shape into small round or oval portions, or press into traditional Sandesh moulds. *Garnish with pistachios and chill briefly before serving. Lapsi A comforting dessert popular in Rajasthan and Gujarat, Lapsi is traditionally prepared during festivals, auspicious occasions and family celebrations. Its nutty flavour, soft, grainy texture and aroma of ghee make it particularly enjoyable during winter. . Ingredients (serves 4) *1 cup coarse broken wheat (dalia) *½ cup ghee *¾ cup grated jaggery *3 cups water *¼ tsp cardamom powder *2 tbsp chopped almonds and cashews *1 tbsp raisins Method *Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add broken wheat and roast over low heat until golden brown and aromatic. *Meanwhile, in a separate pan, dissolve jaggery in warm water and strain to remove impurities. *Carefully add the jaggery water to the roasted wheat. *Cover and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the wheat softens and absorbs the liquid. *Add cardamom powder, raisins and nuts. Mix well. *Serve warm, garnished with a little extra ghee and chopped nuts.

briefs.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled top lawyer on affair with Alice Huang: report
briefs.deck: During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in ‌response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice ​Huang, Jensen Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate
briefs.bodyText:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the company’s leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter andCchief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters.
Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.
On Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry’s heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.
He apologised in a statement for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, whom the U.S. was investigating for potentially spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related.
The New York Times earlier this week reported Mr. Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Mr. Huang had another intimate relationship with a different Nvidia employee.
Mr. Teter did not respond to a request for comment. Mr. Wagonfeld did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for ex-CEO Huang and an Nvidia spokesperson declined to comment. A phone call and email to contact information listed on a business card for Alice Huang went unanswered.
During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, Mr. Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ones from 2025.
In two separate messages in October, Mr. Huang told Nvidia leaders that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers. In other messages, Mr. Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed.
Nvidia’s Mr. Huang also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.
That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe as an affair, the people said. Ultimately, neither Nvidia nor Mr. Huang filed a lawsuit against the paper. A spokesperson for the New York Times said the paper received no legal demand.
It is unclear when his relationship with Alice Huang became intimate. Photos posted online and verified by Reuters show them together in the U.S., China and elsewhere, dating as far back as December 2023.
On November 10, the independent members of Nvidia’s board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Mr. Huang’s relations with Alice Huang, as well as U.S. authorities’ suspicions that she was spying for China. Beijing has denied she is a spy.
Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government.
Jensen Huang said in an interview with Bloomberg published on October 29 that the U.S. government had not informed him about its suspicions regarding Alice Huang.
Nvidia’s stock has fallen more than 30% since its October 6 closing high, erasing more than $1.8 trillion from its market capitalization.

Democratic U.S. senators order Musk to preserve records on Ukraine Starlink access
briefs.deck: Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for frontline communications and ‌drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks
briefs.bodyText:
Democratic U.S. senators have told Elon Musk to preserve all records related to his company SpaceX’s restrictions on Ukraine’s use of its Starlink and Starshield satellite services.
Ukrainian forces say Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, is vital for frontline communications and drone operations in their defense against Russian drone and missile attacks.
But in mid-October, Ukrainian officials complained that the service had been restricted without explanation or warning, limiting their military’s ability to conduct complicated strike missions against Russian forces and slowing interceptor drones used to shoot down Russian attack drones.
“The October and November restrictions now raise the disturbing possibility that these vulnerabilities persist even within systems on which the U.S. government relies,” Senators Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire and Chris Coons of Delaware said in a letter to Mr. Musk.
They gave Mr. Musk until November 30 to provide written confirmation that “all appropriate preservation measures have been implemented.”
The lawmakers sought SpaceX’s records since September 1, including all communications related to Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine as well as communications between Musk, SpaceX executives and the White House and Pentagon.
Shaheen and Coons said the restrictions raised “serious questions” about SpaceX’s control over communications systems critical to national security and criticized what they described as “opaque decision-making.”
Reuters reported in October that an order to limit Starshield service used by Ukrainian forces came from inside the White House. Secretary of State Marco Rubio disputed that account, saying decisions on Ukraine’s access to the service were up to SpaceX and Musk.
Later that month Ukraine said Starlink and Starshield were operating normally. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Thursday (November 12, 2026), however, that Ukrainian military units had again recorded disruptions to Starshield communications.

briefs.headline: Not just another coffee break
Keralam government sanctions ₹11 crore for road development in Kochi
briefs.deck: The project aims to improve the motorability of the road and address hardships faced by commuters, says Ernakulam MLA
briefs.bodyText:
The State government has approved and allocated funds for M.G. Road renovation works and the development of Chinmaya Cross Road, which forms part of the approach road for the proposed Perandoor-Vaduthala bridge project in the Ernakulam Assembly constituency, said T.J. Vinod, MLA.
An amount of ₹6 crore has been allocated for the M.G. Road renovation work, while ₹5 crore has been sanctioned for the development of Chinmaya Cross Road, including land acquisition. The stretch between Madhava Pharmacy Junction and Thevara along M.G. Road will be resurfaced. A cross drain, which is currently dysfunctional, will also be reconstructed as part of the work. The project aims to improve the motorability of the road and address hardships faced by commuters, said Mr. Vinod in a statement issued here.
Main reason for waterlogging
“Skewed slopes of drains remain the main reason for waterlogging along M.G. Road. The PWD (Roads) has submitted a comprehensive project worth ₹20 crore for the development of M.G. Road, including the scientific correction of drain slopes and improvement of footpath. Waterlogging along M.G. Road can be permanently resolved once these works are also implemented,” he said.
Initially, Swagatham Road was identified as the approach road for the Perandoor-Vaduthala bridge. However, it was replaced by Chinmaya Cross Road following widespread complaints from residents that the narrow width of Swagatham Road would lead to traffic congestion once the bridge becomes a reality. The development of Chinmaya Cross Road, including land acquisition for the approach road, will help improve transportation facilities in the area, Mr. Vinod said.
The proposed works have been included in the budgeted works and sanctioned as part of efforts to improve the basic infrastructure of the city’s main roads and address perennial issues such as traffic congestion and waterlogging, he said.

briefs.headline: U.S. loses measles-free status after continued spread of the disease: report
briefs.deck: The reported decision by the Americas branch of the ‌World Health Organization comes as the U.S. battles ‌the ⁠highest number of measles cases it has seen ⁠in more than three decades
briefs.bodyText:
The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the United States’ measles-elimination status after 26 years, because the country did not halt continuous transmission of the highly contagious virus for more than a year, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The international health body did not immediately respond to a request from Reuters for comment on the report, which cited people familiar with the matter.
The reported decision by the Americas branch of the World Health Organization comes as the U.S. battles the highest number of measles cases it has seen in more than three decades.
Some 7,500 people in the U.S. have been infected with measles and 13 have died since 2025. That period coincides with falling immunization rates and rising vaccine hesitancy under U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has for years spread doubts, without scientific evidence, about the safety of measles vaccines.
As part of its evaluation, PAHO reviewed epidemiological and laboratory evidence to determine whether the same strain of measles had been circulating in the United States uninterrupted for 12 months or longer, a sign of local transmission rather than imported cases.
As of Thursday (November 12, 2026), 5,182 confirmed cases of measles had been reported in 2026 to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention from 45 States, New York City and the District of Columbia, surpassing last year’s total of 2,289, making it one of the country’s worst measles resurgences in decades.
The U.S. achieved its measles-elimination status in 2000. A country can halt transmission when 95% of its population is vaccinated, creating so-called herd immunity that also protects those unable to receive the vaccine.
Two doses of the measles vaccine — by far the best way to prevent infection and transmission — provide 97% protection against the virus, which can cause blindness, deafness, brain damage or death.

stories.headline: Global investment, NRI affairs dept to rope in external agency
stories.deck: Karnataka's newly formed department of global investment and NRI affairs is planning to expand its operations abroad. It aims to attract investments by hiring consultants and engaging with NRIs from Karnataka. The department will focus on health, education, and tourism sectors while seeking private equity and family offices. CM DK Shivakumar will oversee the department's operations without…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Two months after its creation, Karnataka's department of global investment and NRI affairs has made a quiet start and now plans to expand abroad. It will hire consultants for three years and rope in a leading global financial consulting firm to attract investments.
Applications opened Thursday, with the finance department clearing posts, department secretary SS Nakul told TOI. Candidates should be fluent in English and have relevant experience. The consultants will handhold investors, engage with NRIs from Karnataka and be the face of destination Karnataka worldwide.
The consulting firm will be picked via a tender, after which specific proposals will be pursued aggressively. While industries and IT-BT departments have their own systems to woo investors, the new department will focus on health, education and tourism. "We will look at private equity, venture capital and family offices for those sectors," Nakul said. It will also seek more funding from businesses already in the state.
CM to oversee affairs
Officials suggested there is no proposal for a separate minister, and the department will stay with CM DK Shivakumar. 
It has so far facilitated his meetings with Poland PM Donald Tusk, Sweden's ambassador Petra Menander and Switzerland's Maya Tiffasi.
"We will soon meet ambassadors and French ministers," Nakul said.
With a budget of Rs 20 crore, the department has only a secretary, deputy secretary and under-secretary. "It will be lean and nimble," Nakul said.
On diaspora welfare, former NRI Forum chairperson Arathi Krishna said she used her diplomatic and NRI networks to help Kannadigas stranded abroad or those who lost jobs since no support structure existed. "The department needs human resources and proper funding to sustain it," she said.
Reskilling project
There is no plan to find re-employment for those fired abroad, but they are being referred to the skills department. "They are being reskilled for jobs suited to India or the countries they plan to move to," Nakul said.

stories.headline: Rajya Sabha panel visits ISRO, HAL facilities in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Members of the Subordinate Legislation Committee of Rajya Sabha on Friday visited key defence, space and finance institutions in Bengaluru as part of a study visit.
The committee, led by Chairman Milind Deora, visited the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), toured the LCA Tejas Division and witnessed a static display of the defence PSU’s various platforms.
The HAL said the committee reviewed the implementation of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014.
“HAL Chairman Ravi K., and Director (HR), M.G. Balasubrahmanya, and other senior officials were present during the interaction, which provided an opportunity to showcase the HAL’s contributions to indigenous aerospace development and its commitment to impactful and sustainable CSR initiatives,” the HAL said.
The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies.
“The committee got a closer look at India’s satellite capabilities and discussed the future of our space sector from liberalisation and reusable rockets to Chandrayaan missions, space debris and e-waste regulations. While India’s space ambitions are reaching new heights, our sustainability game must keep up. Innovation and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” Mr. Deora posted on X.
The committee also held meetings with officials of the Reserve Bank of India and leading Public Sector Unit (PSU) banks to discuss the future of digital payment security.

stories.headline: Bengaluru Pink Line begins operations today; BMRCL announces timings as commuters seek faster completion of underground section
stories.bodyText:
Train services on the elevated section of Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and S.G. Palya will commence on Saturday, the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) announced on Friday, following its inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
However, the opening of the partial stretch has drawn mixed reactions from commuters, with several pointing out that the elevated section alone is unlikely to make a significant difference to the city’s overall metro connectivity. They have urged the BMRCL to expedite the completion and opening of the underground section, which is crucial to connecting south Bengaluru with the Central Business District (CBD) and north Bengaluru.
Schedule
According to the schedule released by the BMRCL, the first train on Mondays will depart from Kalena Agrahara at 4.55 a.m., while services from S.G. Palya will begin at 5 a.m. From Tuesday to Saturday, the first trains will operate from both terminal stations at 6 a.m. On Sundays, services will commence at 7 a.m.
The early start on Mondays is intended to accommodate passengers arriving in Bengaluru from other parts of the State after the weekend, officials said. The last train will depart from Kalena Agrahara at 10.50 p.m. and from S.G. Palya at 10.54 p.m.
Frequency
Trains will operate at eight-minute intervals during peak hours from Monday to Friday. During non-peak hours on weekdays, the frequency will be 10 minutes. On Saturdays and Sundays, trains will run every 10 minutes throughout operating hours.
The BMRCL said the frequency of services would be revised depending on passenger traffic patterns.
Limited benefits
Manjunath K., a resident of Hulimavu, also questioned the operational schedule, stating that the timings indicated the BMRCL’s expectations of relatively low ridership on the partial stretch.
“The way the BMRCL has announced the timings for the Pink Line shows that it is expecting low ridership. They know that opening a small stretch will not have a major impact on passenger numbers. However, commuters travelling towards the Green and Yellow lines can interchange at the Jayadeva Hospital Metro Station and reach other destinations. The connectivity to the CBD and north Bengaluru, which is the primary purpose of this line, is still not fulfilled,” he said.
Meanwhile, the BMRCL has fixed fares on the operational section of the Pink Line between ₹10 and ₹30, depending on the distance travelled. Passengers travelling from Suddagunte Palya to Kalena Agrahara will have to pay ₹30.
Five feeder routes
In a move to strengthen last-mile connectivity, the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) will introduce five dedicated feeder bus services connecting key Pink Line Metro stations with nearby residential and commercial areas from November 14. The services will cover neighbourhoods including Hulimavu, Tavarekere, J.P. Nagar and Uttarahalli. A total of 28 buses will operate 401 trips across the five routes.
The routes include services from the Jayadeva Hospital Metro Station to Uttarahalli, feeder connections between Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere, a circular service from J.P. Nagar 4th Phase Metro Station, a route connecting Hulimavu and Singasandra, and another circular service from the Tavarekere Metro Station.
The BMTC and the BMRCL have jointly installed LED displays at Tavarekere and IIMB metro stations to provide real-time estimated arrival times of the connecting BMTC buses. The facility is expected to be extended to other metro stations in phases.

stories.headline: Mysuru gets India’s first tilted 8K LED dome planetarium
stories.deck: COSMOS, the inaugural LED dome planetarium of India, has opened its doors in Mysuru with an investment of Rs 115 crore. This state-of-the-art facility boasts a 160-seat sky theatre equipped with cutting-edge LED technology, showcasing vibrant visuals. Visitors can immerse themselves in an in-house film detailing the rich history and astronomy of Mysuru, available in various languages.
stories.bodyText:
MYSURU: The city is now home to India’s first tilted 8K LED dome planetarium, with Prime Minister 
Narendra Modi
 inaugurating the Rs 115 crore COSMOS facility at the foothills of Chamundi Hill here Friday.
The 160-seater planetarium, jointly developed by Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) and University of Mysore, is one of its kind in the world in terms of its massive active pixel array and real-time data integration.
Unlike conventional planetariums that rely on projectors, COSMOS uses individually controlled LED panels to produce high-resolution visuals. The dome’s 6,150 individually controlled LED panels carry 4.2 crore pixels, higher than the standard 8K benchmark, producing ultra high-contrast images seamlessly across the 15-metre diameter curved surface.
Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Modi stressed the need to prioritise scientific research, innovation and opportunities for young people. He said opening up the space sector to private players had enabled companies and start-ups to develop and launch rockets and satellites.
“Our satellites help fishermen, track trains real time, and provide data for crop insurance,” the PM added.
The sky theatre at the planetarium will also screen an in-house film exploring the links between Mysuru’s history and astronomy, with shows in Kannada, English and Hindi.
Union finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
 described the facility as an important addition to Mysuru’s tradition of learning and scholarship. “India’s first LED dome planetarium brings many important benefits. COSMOS makes astronomy accessible through an immersive learning experience. It helps children understand stars and planets and encourages them to ask questions,” she said.
Chief minister 
D K Shivakumar
 announced Karnataka govt’s support for a proposed COSMOS centre at Hampi, stressing the need to decentralise scientific infrastructure.
With Kannada content and student mentorship, COSMOS is expected to take science education to rural schools.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru joins 100km Metro club as PM flags off Pink Line stretch; underground section likely to open next year
briefs.deck: Bengaluru's Metro network has now surpassed 100 kilometers following the inauguration of the new Pink Line stretch. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the elevated portion connecting Kalena Agrahara to SG Palya on November 14. The commercial operations of this 7.5-km segment began the same day, with fares ranging from Rs 10 to Rs 30. Future plans include completing the remaining underground…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: India’s tech capital Friday joined the 100-km Metro rail network club, with the inauguration of a 7.5-km stretch of the Pink Line that took its operational network to 103km -- the country’s second-largest after Delhi (416km). Mumbai is third with 101km of operational network.
PM 
Narendra Modi
, who inaugurated the elevated stretch between Kalena Agrahara and SG Palya, said: “We’ve been continuously scoring centuries. After Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru has become the third city in the country to cross the 100km Metro network mark.”
Modi also virtually flagged off the Bengaluru-Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express.
BMRCL will begin commercial operations on the new Metro stretch from today (Nov 14). Fares will range from Rs 10 to Rs 30 for the six-stations that are now operational. BMRCL plans to deploy five trainsets, with one on standby. Trains will initially run at eight-minute intervals during peak hours.
The elevated section is part of the 21-km Pink Line, connecting Kalena Agrahara in the south to Nagawara in the north. The remaining underground section on this line between Dairy Circle and Nagawara is expected to open next year.
Modi spoke at IIM-B after flagging off the inaugural train from SG Palya near Dairy Circle. The Centre, he said, has prioritised infrastructure development in Bengaluru, recognising its role as an engine of economic growth and innovation, Modi.
He travelled to the Bilekahalli-IIMB station, accompanied by chief minister DK Shivakumar, Governor Sudha Yadav, and other dignitaries. The PM used a National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) for the journey.
The PM began his address by greeting the gathering in Kannada. Before boarding, the PM was briefed on the Metro network, ongoing projects and passenger information systems, including real-time BMTC bus arrival updates near Metro stations to help commuters plan their onward journeys.
Six-level structure at Jayadeva
Shivakumar and Greater Bengaluru Development minister Krishna Byre Gowda explained the engineering complexities of the six-level structure at the Jayadeva interchange station, which integrates the Pink and Yellow lines with a double-decker road. At 38 metres, it is among the tallest Metro stations in the country and has been designed as a major multimodal interchange point.
Jayadeva will be Bengaluru’s third major Metro interchange after Majestic and RV Road. It is expected to improve connectivity along Bannerghatta Road, linking commuters to the Electronics City corridor through the Yellow Line and the central business district.
Nine years in the making
Friday’s inauguration marked a milestone for residents along the corridor, but the wait has been long. Sanctioned 12 years ago and taken up for construction in 2017, the elevated stretch took nine years to complete.
PM hails push for energy security
Modi said the recently introduced Vande Bharat Sleeper service between Bengaluru and Mumbai would boost rail connectivity in Karnataka. He also highlighted station redevelopment under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, aimed at providing airport-like facilities and modern amenities.
On energy security, he cited the Mangaluru LPG project, Devangonthi marketing terminal, and a Bengaluru compressed biogas plant set to produce 13 tonnes daily.
Highlighting solar initiatives, Modi said over 60 lakh households, including more than 40,000 in Karnataka, had installed rooftop solar panels under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, receiving around Rs 80,000 in central assistance per household.
Commercial run from today

- New elevated section between Kalena Agrahara and SG Palya has 6 stations
- Commercial operations begin today
- Fares from Rs 10-30 and trains at eight-minute intervals during peak hours
- Remaining underground stretch between Dairy Circle and Nagawara likely to open in 2027
- Six-level Jayadeva interchange, at 38 metres, integrates Pink and Yellow lines with a double-decker road
- It connects Bannerghatta Road to Electronics City and the CBD
- Elevated stretch, sanctioned 12 years ago, took 9 years to complete

briefs.headline: Karnataka launches three-month pilot of menopause health programme in Dakshina Kannada
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The state govt has ordered a three-month pilot of its midlife women’s health and menopause programme, Ruthu Taare, in Dakshina Kannada district, offering dedicated clinics and comprehensive screening for women aged 35 and above.
The programme will cover perimenopausal, menopausal and post-menopausal women, addressing health concerns that often go undiagnosed or are dismissed as part of ageing. Services will include screening for non-communicable diseases and cancers, mental health assessments, nutrition counselling and referrals. “Women’s health does not end with motherhood, and menopause should never be a journey women are expected to endure in silence,” health minister UT Khader said.
As per the health department commissionerate’s Nov 12 order, dedicated clinic sessions will be held every Wednesday at primary health centres, taluk hospitals and district hospitals. Designated medical colleges may hold Saturday clinics, subject to feasibility and personnel availability. Screening will cover hypertension, diabetes, obesity, other cardiometabolic risk factors, and breast and cervical cancers.
 A midlife health card will record screening results, clinical assessments, investigations, referrals and follow-up.
A green-yellow-red risk classification system will identify women needing different levels of mental health support, with links to existing services, including Gruha Arogya.Nutrition counselling will cover balanced diets, adequate protein and calcium intake, locally available nutritious food, bone health, osteoporosis prevention and healthy weight management.
District health authorities must map healthcare facilities, identify participating centres and assess infrastructure, personnel and specialist referral services. ASHAs, ASHA mentors, community health officers, medical officers and nursing staff will be trained.
The district health officer will submit monthly progress reports. After three months, the pilot will be evaluated on screening coverage, referral completion, service availability, operational feasibility and resource requirements. Officials said findings would inform proposals to refine the programme and expand it across Karnataka in phases.
Karnataka is also developing a dedicated women’s health policy, initially focusing on menopause, and plans a one-year menopause fellowship to create a specialist workforce.
Actress and former MP 
Ramya
, Ruthu Taare’s ambassador, welcomed the initiative on X, saying, “Menopause is finally on the public health map.”

briefs.headline: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar seeks fairer Centre-state division in Bengaluru Metro funding
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Seeking greater financial commitment from the Centre towards Namma Metro, chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 Friday called for a fairer division of investment between the Centre and the state, arguing that 
Karnataka
 has been bearing a higher financial burden despite the project being structured as a 50:50 partnership.
The demand was made in the presence of Prime Minister 
Narendra Modi
 at the inauguration of the elevated section of the Pink Line. Ahead of the inauguration, Karnataka govt had claimed that the state has borne 84% of Namma Metro’s project cost. The claim triggered a war of words between Congress and BJP functionaries, with BJP rejecting govt’s assessment and arguing that the Centre had extended substantial financial support to the project.
“I have drawn up several plans to address Bengaluru’s traffic problems, and Metro connectivity is one of the most critical components. Though Metro projects are implemented on a 50:50 partnership basis between the Centre and the state, the actual financial burden on the state govt is much higher,” Shivakumar said.
Pointing to the high cost of foreign borrowings, he said Metro projects should be financed through national banks and other financial institutions at more affordable interest rates. 
He also sought a mechanism for the Centre and states to share operational cash losses and foreign exchange risks arising from external loans.
The chief minister also sought faster clearances for Metro projects, particularly the proposed Red Line connecting Sarjapur and Hebbal, which has been awaiting central approval for more than two years. He called for time-bound approvals, regular reviews under the PRAGATI mechanism and Prime Minister’s direct intervention to resolve delays in approvals.
Shivakumar said project costs should be assessed based on the actual conditions in individual cities rather than uniform national averages. He pointed out that detailed project reports were often two to three years old by the time they received central approval and proposed that cost escalations arising from such delays be shared by the Centre and state.
He also proposed establishing a dedicated national technical institution for Metro projects to provide technical guidance, promote advanced technologies and speed up decision-making.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru Metro’s Pink Line opens to cheers and smiles: Locals say no more time will be lost in congestion
briefs.deck: Vindhya Pabolu & Anush S
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: After a decade of waiting, bumpy rides, endless delays and prolonged uncertainty, the Pink Line Metro was finally inaugurated partially Friday morning, offering residents of Bannerghatta Road a glimpse of relief from their daily commuting woes. The concrete viaducts, which had stood empty for over a year, finally came to life as trains began chugging along the much-anticipated stretch.
For over a decade, commuters had navigated multiple junctions amid dust from Metro construction. Pillars stood surrounded by garbage, while construction debris piled up on footpaths and the pothole-ridden carriageway. 
TOI had repeatedly highlighted these issues and the hardships faced by motorists.
The run-up to the inaugural journey, however, saw a festive atmosphere, with hundreds of people lining the road to catch a glimpse of the decked-up train carrying 
Prime Minister Narendra Modi
 and chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
. Around SG Palya station, where the PM boarded the train, residents thronged the streets as convoys carrying top political figures passed by amid cheers.
TOI spoke to residents and commuters to find out how the Pink Line would change their daily journeys. Here’s what they had to say:
Gajan Naik | Basavanagudi resident
I’m a freelance graphic designer, so I travel here and there for my work. But because of this Metro, connectivity will increase now and traffic will also come down. There’ll be no need for many people to plan an hour in advance to go somewhere
Veena Basavaraj | commuter
We’ve waited a long time for this Metro line to open. Until now, the Metro only went as far as 
MG Road
 or JP Nagar 6th Phase, and for everything else we struggled with autos, bikes, our own cars or buses, even for short distances. Now the Metro is within walking distance. If I want to go to Vega City for some fun, I no longer have to wait, book a ride and pay high fares. I can just take the Metro. It will also help a lot of students in this area
Baby Shalini | JP Nagar resident
This Metro is helpful in this heavy traffic; if it is extended up to Bannerghatta, it will benefit more people. We usually get stuck near Vega City mall while commuting back from work
Anasuya A | commuter to NS Palya
There is heavy traffic during peak hours along this road; this Metro needs an extension southwards also. I was actually very excited to see the train running through the track; we were also expecting a roadshow from Modi
Sasikala V | Bilekahalli resident
From morning, many people including me waited for 3-4 hours in the heat to catch a glimpse of Modiji; it has been my dream to meet him. The Metro opening brings a lot of joy to us residents
Pallavi Ramnathkar | homemaker
Whenever I go shopping near MG Road or in any other area, I usually have to take a taxi, because my nearest Metro station is 1.5-2km from me. But now, because of Pink Line, the Metro station is literally 200 metres from where I live. I can just walk there and then go anywhere else. This is really convenient for me. It will help me save a lot of money, and there’s no need to plan hours in advance
Sirajsuresh S | retired bank employee
I’ve heard from friends that many IT people struggle when it comes to commuting in this part of the city... people always complain about expensive taxis. With Pink Line’s launch, such people will benefit; everyone can save a lot of money, and it will help with the traffic as well

briefs.headline: Bengaluru school booked for cutting 12 tree branches sans permission
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Greater Bengaluru Authority’s forest department has registered an FIR against Auro Mirra International School at Ulsoor after it allegedly cut 12 branches of two trees on its premises without obtaining prior permission. The school, however, has defended the pruning, saying it was undertaken as a safety measure to protect students.
Following an inspection, the department registered a tree cutting offence case against a person associated with the school on Nov 11.
According to the range forest officer (RFO), branches of a peepal tree and a gulmohar tree were cut without prior approval from the department. The case has been registered under the Karnataka Preservation of Trees Act, 1976.
The matter was also taken to the additional chief judicial magistrate’s court which authorised the forest department to investigate the alleged non-cognisable offence and submit a final report.
The RFO said the investigation was under way and that the school could either pay the prescribed penalty after the investigation or approach the court for further proceedings.
A school representative said a large branch of the gulmohar tree had fallen while children were lining up for the school assembly, narrowly avoiding an accident. 
The school also claimed that the branches removed were leaning towards the building and terrace.
“We have a campus built around trees, and every plant and tree is important to us. We have trees that are nearly 200 years old, and we have been protecting them. The branches were cut only from a safety perspective, as some were leaning towards the building,” the representative said.
When 
TOI
 asked why permission was not sought, the representative said the campus manager was on leave and not available to comment.
Meanwhile, residents have sought stringent action against the school, arguing that unauthorised pruning of mature trees could affect the city’s urban bird population.

briefs.headline: Coorg’s avocado curries, her father’s plantation visit and Ballari’s politics in Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging
briefs.deck: From Amie aunty’s stories of Coorg and her father’s visit to an arecanut plantation to her own electoral contest in Ballari, Sonia Gandhi’s Belonging: A Journey of Love traces the many ways Karnataka became part of her family’s story and political journey
briefs.bodyText:
An arecanut plantation in Karnataka was among the places that caught the interest of Sonia Gandhi’s father, Stefano Maino, during his visits to India. Alongside a power project in Keralam and a factory in Maharashtra, it was one of the places he chose to see beyond the usual tourist circuit, writes Sonia Gandhi in her recently released memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, remembering her father as a formidable patriarch, “loved, respected, feared” within the family.
From her father’s visits to India and the memories of people who became part of her family life to the electoral contests in which she and her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, were involved, Karnataka finds mention in different parts of the memoir.
Amie aunty
Another person from Karnataka who figures in Sonia Gandhi’s memories of the people who made the Gandhi household feel like home was Amie Crishna, who hailed from Coorg and served as one of Indira Gandhi’s personal secretaries. Amie aunty, as Sonia Gandhi came to call her, had known Indira Gandhi since her early days at Teen Murti House.
The two would go to the “bazar” together to look for things Indira Gandhi needed. Amie, Sonia Gandhi writes, would also tell her about Coorg, its people and their valour, and its food, including “curries made with the avocados that grew wild there”. She writes of how fond she grew of Amie aunty, whom she describes as “a sunny, loving and lovable human being” and a “trusted elder aunt”.
Two electoral battles
The State also figures in the electoral journeys of both Indira Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi.
Sonia Gandhi recalls how the coffee-growing constituency of Chikkamagaluru gave her mother-in-law a route back to Parliament in November 1978, after her defeat in Rae Bareli in the 1977 Lok Sabha election in the aftermath of the Emergency. As she notes, Chikkamagaluru was among the southern constituencies that continued to support her mother-in-law even as much of the North had turned against her. Indira Gandhi won the byelection comfortably and returned to the Lok Sabha.
Karnataka also became the setting for Sonia Gandhi’s own electoral debut. In 1999, she contested from Amethi, the constituency represented by Rajiv Gandhi. Her senior Congress colleagues, however, urged her to enter the fray from a southern constituency as well, amid apprehensions that the BJP might find a way to keep her out of Parliament by getting the Amethi election countermanded. What she describes as a “cat-and-mouse game” brought her to Ballari.
The BJP and the RSS, on learning of the plan, chose Sushma Swaraj to take her on. Their calculation, Sonia Gandhi writes, was that Ms. Swaraj would keep her occupied in Ballari, even if she did not win, leaving her with less time to campaign in Amethi and elsewhere in the country. Ms. Swaraj, she writes, also added a local touch and soon began picking up Kannada phrases and framed the contest as one between the “desi beti” and the “videshi bahu”.
The memoir also recounts how Sonia Gandhi, then relatively new to electoral politics, was unfamiliar with Ballari. Her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, accompanied her when she filed her nominations in both constituencies and joined her on the campaign trail in Ballari.
Sonia Gandhi travelled through Ballari’s “dry and rocky” landscape with local party leaders and stayed at the partially built house of a Congress supporter. His wife, she writes, “would pop up periodically, smilingly offering a plate laden with freshly made tidbits that I felt compelled to accept, even if I wasn’t hungry.”
The election result, Sonia Gandhi said, surprised her. She won both the Ballari and Amethi constituencies, but had to choose one of the two seats. As she writes, “Inevitably, I chose Amethi.”

stories.headline: US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US-bound services
stories.deck: Travelers on Air India flights faced significant delays due to a nationwide communication failure that affected the FAA, leading to a temporary ground halt of all flight departures across the U.S. Although the ground stop has since been lifted, passengers should brace for ongoing disruptions as the situation unfolds. Investigations are in progress to pinpoint the cause behind this communication…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Air India
 flights operating to and from the US could face disruptions after a communication outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a nationwide ground stop on departures.
The airline said the disruption had affected departures from airports across the country, potentially impacting its US operations. It has advised passengers to check their flight status before setting out for the airport and plan their travel accordingly.
"A nationwide ground stop is currently in effect across the US due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. As a result, departures from airports across US are impacted, with possible consequential disruptions to Air India flights to and from the US," the airline wrote on X.
Air India said its teams were monitoring the situation closely and would provide further updates as they became available.
However, the ground stop has now been lifted according to Reuters, but the disruption is likely to continue.
The chaos follows the FAA's had halted departures across the country on Friday after a telecommunications outage affected regional air traffic control operations. The restriction brought departures to a standstill at airports across the US, leaving thousands of passengers facing disrupted travel plans.
The FAA said the decision was taken "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".
The outage affected all 22 regional air route traffic control centres, which direct aircraft travelling between airports. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said FAA technicians were investigating the problem, while the agency maintained that the communication disruption made it unsafe for flights to continue departing normally.
Also Read| 
US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so far
Network router problem suspected
The precise cause of the outage remained under investigation. However, according to an airline source cited by CNN, the FAA informed carriers that a problem with network routers had triggered the disruption. The issue was believed to have started at Chicago Midway International Airport before spreading across the country.
During initial crisis discussions, the FAA was reportedly unable to give a clear explanation of the problem. Different facilities were experiencing the outage in different ways.
Homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said the problem appeared to be related to telecommunications. Officials had no indication that it was the result of an attack, although authorities were examining the communication systems used by air traffic controllers.
Also Read| 
Trump rules out cyberattack, AI as US probes nationwide flight disruption
The ground stop prevented aircraft from taking off, but flights that were already airborne were allowed to continue to their destinations and land. Officials said they were assessing aircraft still in the air on a case-by-case basis.
The nationwide suspension was the first since January 2023, when a malfunction in a key FAA computer system disrupted flight operations. It was also only the second such order since the September 11, 2001, attacks.

stories.headline: Tata feud: Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh hit back at Khambata, accuse him of ignoring governance failures
stories.deck: In a five-page letter, the two Vice-Chairmen of Tata Trusts said opposition to listing Tata Sons should not be driven by a wish to keep control in the Trusts’ leadership’s hands
stories.bodyText:
Tata Trusts Vice-Chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh have launched a strong rebuttal to fellow trustee Darius Khambata’s criticism of the Tata Sons board’s September 17, 2026 decisions, accusing him of presenting an incomplete account of the dispute. They have questioned whether his opposition to listing the group holding company is driven by the interests of the Tata institutions or by a desire to keep control in the hands of the Trusts’ present leadership.
In a five-page letter dated November 11, 2026, the two trustees challenged Mr. Khambata’s arguments on the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) regulatory position, the proposed listing of Tata Sons, the fiduciary responsibilities of Trust nominees, and the circumstances surrounding the reappointment of Chairman N. Chandrasekaran.
They also questioned his account of the events leading to the September board meeting, asking why he had not objected when an earlier unanimous decision to renew Mr. Chandrasekaran’s tenure was allowed to remain unresolved for seven months.
The unusually direct exchange exposes the depth of divisions within the Tata Trusts, which collectively hold about 66% of Tata Sons, the holding company of the $277 billion conglomerate. At stake is not merely whether Tata Sons should remain privately held, but also the balance of authority between its controlling charitable shareholders and the company’s board.
Trusts Chairman Noel Tata and Mr. Khambata have opposed Mr. Chandrasekaran’s reappointment for another five-year term and resisted listing Tata Sons, arguing that a public listing could undermine the distinctive governance structure of the Tata Group and the Trusts’ ability to safeguard its long-term interests.
Mr. Srinivasan and Mr. Singh, however, have backed the board’s decision to reappoint Mr. Chandrasekaran, and argued that the company must respect regulatory requirements, including the RBI’s listing framework.
RBI decision cannot be blamed on advocacy
On the central question of listing, the two rejected Mr. Khambata’s contention that Tata Sons’ engagement with the RBI had been neither meaningful nor successful. They said discussions with the regulator began in 2023, leading to the repayment of debt and an application for deregistration in March 2024, and continued thereafter. Trustees had been kept informed throughout, and none had questioned the adequacy of the engagement at the time, they said.
The RBI’s decision after a two-year review, that Tata Sons must continue to comply with the regulatory framework for upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), could not be attributed to inadequate advocacy, they argued. “If, by ‘meaningful’ advocacy, you mean advocacy that secures preferential treatment or circumvents the applicable rules, then that would not be consistent with the Tata model you seek to uphold,” they wrote.
The RBI rejected Tata Sons’ application to surrender its NBFC registration in September 2026, effectively closing the route the company had pursued to avoid the listing requirement. The holding company had repaid more than ₹21,000 crore in debt before seeking deregistration in March 2024.
Listing versus the Tata model
The two trustees disputed Mr. Khambata’s assertion that listing Tata Sons would pose an existential threat to the charitable Trusts or the Tata model. They cited overseas companies, including Novo Nordisk, Hershey, Lundbeck and Demant, which have foundation or trust-linked ownership structures despite being publicly listed.
Within the Tata Group, they pointed to Tata Consultancy Services, Tata Steel, Tata Power and Tata Motors as examples of listed companies undertaking large, long-term investments. “Disclosure and accountability bring discipline to how capital is allocated; they do not limit vision,” they said.
They argued that listing would not sever the relationship between Tata Sons and the Trusts, which would continue as shareholders and retain their entitlement to dividends that fund charitable activities. Invoking the late Ratan Tata’s creed, “Whatever India needs”, they said national service must also encompass respect for the country’s laws and institutions, including the RBI.
In one of the sharpest passages, they questioned whether the opposition to listing was genuinely about preserving the Tata model or about retaining control over Tata Sons. They also argued that the Trusts’ tax-exempt status and public purpose required them to prioritise their charitable objects rather than control of a commercial enterprise.
Dispute over trustees’ role and board independence
Mr. Srinivasan and Mr. Singh challenged Mr. Khambata’s interpretation of the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Tata-Mistry dispute, particularly his argument on the obligations of Trust-nominated directors. They said the judgment had upheld Tata Sons’ Articles of Association and the legitimate exercise of powers by its board and majority, but had not extinguished directors’ fiduciary obligations to the company, or turned Trust nominees into delegates required to follow the Trusts’ instructions regardless of the company’s interests.
Mechanically requiring nominees to vote according to the Trusts’ position would undermine independent board judgment and the principle of corporate democracy, they argued.
The trustees also revisited a September 11, 2025 vote in which four trustees, including Mr. Khambata, opposed renewing Mr. Singh’s tenure as a Trust nominee director on the Tata Sons board. Mr. Khambata had described the decision as necessary to strengthen opposition to listing and preserve the Trusts’ veto.
The two argued that this effectively made a board appointment contingent on securing a particular voting outcome rather than assessing the nominee’s merit. They added that Tata Sons’ Articles of Association contemplated differences of opinion among Trust-nominated directors and provided a mechanism to resolve them.
Seven months of leadership uncertainty
A substantial part of the letter focuses on the events preceding the September 17, 2026 board meeting, which culminated in Mr. Chandrasekaran’s reappointment for another five-year term. The trustees laid out a chronology beginning on July 28, 2025, when the boards of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust unanimously recommended his reappointment.
Mr. Khambata had supported and, according to the letter, drafted that resolution. They said the position changed after two new trustees were inducted into the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust in November 2025, altering its internal balance.
In February 2026, the earlier recommendation was no longer being acted upon and the reappointment was deferred, and the resulting uncertainty continued for seven months until the Tata Sons board acted on September 17.
They cited a July 10, 2025 communication in which Mr. Khambata had described Mr. Chandrasekaran’s results and future plans as “even more impressive than I’d imagined”, adding that the late Ratan Tata “would have been elated”. They asked what had changed between that assessment and his subsequent opposition, other than the composition of the Trusts.
“A Trustee is free to revise his view, as you accept of others. But one who praised the Chairman in those terms and then stood by passively while his reappointment was left in doubt for seven months, owes the Trusts and the public an explanation,” they wrote.
They also questioned why Mr. Khambata had not objected when earlier Trust resolutions were not implemented, and why he had proposed a trustee induction that, according to them, altered the balance the late Ratan Tata had sought to preserve.
Board’s decision defended
Explaining the September 17 decision, the two said Mr. Chandrasekaran had decided not to seek another term after his current tenure ends in February 2027, following more than six months of uncertainty over his reappointment. They said the board’s Nomination and Remuneration Committee had unanimously asked him to reconsider, while the board was overseeing major investments in semiconductors, batteries, technology and aviation.
The board acted to end an uncertainty it had not created, they argued, rejecting the suggestion that its decision was the origin of the governance crisis.
The reappointment has itself been contested by Trusts Chairman Noel Tata, who has questioned its legality under the Articles of Association. The September 17 vote exposed a split among Trust-nominated directors, with Mr. Srinivasan supporting the reappointment and Mr. Noel Tata opposing it.
The two also accused Mr. Khambata of overlooking the lack of consensus surrounding changes to the composition of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust in November 2025. They invoked Ratan Tata’s decades-long role in building consensus within the two principal trusts, saying his moral authority had been earned through conduct rather than inherited through a designation. “Such authority cannot be inherited. It has to be earned, and it is not conferred by a title or a voting majority,” they wrote.
A deeper institutional crisis
The letter’s broader argument is that the principal threat to the Tata model is not a stock market listing or an assertive board, but the erosion of collective decision-making and institutional independence. “The real threat to the Tata model is neither the listing of Tata Sons nor a Board that exercises independent judgment. It is the weakening of collective governance, the concentration of authority in a few individuals, and the erosion of the institutional independence that Mr. Ratan Tata spent a lifetime building,” they said.
The outcome has implications beyond the immediate leadership dispute. A potential listing would bring greater public disclosure and shareholder scrutiny to the holding company, while continued opposition to listing could intensify questions over how Tata Sons intends to meet the RBI’s regulatory requirements.
The two trustees ended by endorsing Mr. Khambata’s invocation of Ratan Tata’s principle that “the institution is always bigger than the individual” and that “duties are owed to institutions, not to individuals”. The principle must apply equally to every trustee and chairman, they said, calling for a constructive resolution in the interests of the Tata institutions.
